entries.title: Opus 4.8 is the new default · effort labels renamed Faster/Smarter
entries.paragraph: Opus 4.8 is now the default model at high effort. Fast mode on Opus 4.8 runs at 2x the standard rate for ~2.5x throughput. The effort labels formerly shown as Speed / Intelligence are now Faster / Smarter. Also introduces dynamic workflows that orchestrate hundreds of background agents.
entries.whyItMatters: Every dashboard, doc, or script that greps for Speed/Intelligence needs an audit. Auto-bumped CLI installs are silently jumping models — pin if you need 4.7 behavior for reproducibility.

example.code:
# pin if you need 4.7 reproducibility
npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.149

# or scan dotfiles for label renames
rg -F 'Speed|Intelligence' .claude .github docs

entries.title: Opus 4.8 thinking-block fix · CLAUDE_CODE_OPUS_4_6_FAST_MODE_OVERRIDE removal today
entries.paragraph: Fixes a regression where thinking blocks were silently modified on Opus 4.8 and surfaced as API errors. Also announces the removal of the CLAUDE_CODE_OPUS_4_6_FAST_MODE_OVERRIDE env var on 06/01 — today.
entries.whyItMatters: If you have that env var set anywhere (shell rc, CI, Docker), it stops working today and stale assumptions about fast-mode routing will break quietly.

entries.title: Plugins in .claude/skills/ auto-load (no marketplace needed)
entries.paragraph: Anything under .claude/skills/ is now auto-discovered as a plugin without registering a marketplace. Adds claude plugin init <name> scaffolding and /plugin argument autocomplete. Bundle of fixes across MCP, sandbox, agents, worktrees, and terminal rendering.
entries.whyItMatters: Drop-in plugin loading shortens the iteration loop for in-repo skills — no marketplace registration, no separate install step. Repo-local skills become first-class.

example.code:
claude plugin init my-plugin
# scaffolds .claude/skills/my-plugin/ — loaded automatically next session

entries.title: Auto mode on Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry for Opus 4.7 + 4.8
entries.paragraph: Auto mode is now opt-in on Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Azure Foundry for Opus 4.7 and 4.8. Enable via CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1.
entries.whyItMatters: Teams blocked on first-party data residency can now use Auto mode in regulated clouds. No code change — just an env var on the provider you already use.

entries.title: Fix: stdio MCP servers restarting on every reconcile pass
entries.paragraph: A config-equality false positive was causing stdio MCP servers to be torn down and re-spawned on every reconcile pass. Fixed — servers stay up between reconciles.
entries.whyItMatters: If you ship the Agent SDK in a long-running process with stdio MCP servers, you were paying spawn-cost on every reconcile and probably leaking PIDs. Bump and verify your MCP server logs.

entries.title: Parity with Claude Code 2.1.157 (plugin auto-load)
entries.paragraph: Roll-up release matching the underlying CLI behavior for plugin auto-load and the plugin init command. No standalone SDK API changes.
entries.whyItMatters: Pin to this if your hosted-agent users expect the same plugin discovery behavior as the latest CLI.

entries.title: Parity with Claude Code 2.1.158 (Auto mode on Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry)
entries.paragraph: Roll-up release matching the CLI's Auto-mode support on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry behind CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE=1. No SDK API additions.
entries.whyItMatters: Required if you deploy the Agent SDK against Bedrock / Vertex / Foundry and want Auto mode available to your users.

entries.title: Parity with Claude Code 2.1.159
entries.paragraph: Internal-infra parity bump matching CLI v2.1.159. No user-facing API changes.
entries.whyItMatters: Latest pin if you want to stay aligned with the CLI's current internal release line.

entries.title: Legacy profile configs rejected · --profile is now primary
entries.paragraph: --profile becomes the primary profile selector across CLI, TUI, and sandbox flows. Legacy profile configs (the v1 shape) are now hard-rejected with migration guidance. New on top: rollout-backed conversation history search (case-insensitive), per-server env targeting for MCP, OAuth on streamable HTTP MCP servers, parallel calls for MCP tools that declare readOnlyHint, and best-effort compaction of oversized connector tool schemas.
entries.whyItMatters: If you still ship a legacy profile block in config.toml, the CLI now refuses to start until migrated. Read-only MCP parallelism is a quiet perf win for tools that opted into the hint.

example.code:
# old (rejected): top-level [profile.<name>]
# new: explicit --profile selector + per-profile files
codex --profile work

# .codex/profiles/work.toml
[permissions]
network = "deny"
fs_write = ["$WORKSPACE"]

entries.title: codex doctor diagnostics · vim text-objects · named permission-profile picker
entries.paragraph: codex doctor now reports environment, Git, terminal, app-server, and thread inventory — paste-ready for support. /status shows remote connection + server version when connected over a remote transport. Vim mode gained text-object editing and configurable interrupt-turn binding. /permissions understands named permission profiles and shows custom profiles. install.sh/install.ps1 support CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 for CI installs.
entries.whyItMatters: Doctor output replaces 20 minutes of Q&A on support tickets. Non-interactive installer is the missing piece for cleanly bootstrapping Codex in CI images.

example.code:
# CI bootstrap
CODEX_NON_INTERACTIVE=1 curl -fsSL https://codex.openai.com/install.sh | sh

# debug a user's environment in one command
codex doctor > codex-doctor.txt

entries.title: undici dispatcher mismatch guidance · text/plain binary uploads fixed
entries.paragraph: Sharpens the error message when you pass an undici Dispatcher instance that does not match the runtime's undici version. Also treats text/plain responses declared with format: binary as raw uploads instead of decoded text.
entries.whyItMatters: If you mix the SDK with a custom fetchOptions.dispatcher you were probably already chasing this. Bump to skip the debugging.

example.code:
bun add openai@^6.39.1
# or
npm i openai@^6.39.1

entries.title: MCP goes stateless · initialize handshake removed · big deprecation pass
entries.paragraph: Release candidate for the next stable MCP spec (2026-07-28). Removes the initialize / notifications/initialized handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header — every request now carries protocol version, client identity, and capabilities in _meta. Introduces a required server/discover RPC, replaces the GET endpoint and resources/subscribe/unsubscribe with a single subscriptions/listen stream, and removes ping, logging/setLevel, and notifications/roots/list_changed. Roots, Sampling, and Logging features are now deprecated; HTTP+SSE transport reclassified as deprecated.
entries.whyItMatters: Any server you ship that relies on the handshake, session ids, GET-stream subscriptions, or Roots/Sampling/Logging will need a migration plan before the stable cuts. Twelve-month deprecation window starts from the stable release, but SDKs will move at their own pace.

suggestions.title: Today: remove CLAUDE_CODE_OPUS_4_6_FAST_MODE_OVERRIDE from every env
suggestions.paragraph: The override env var is removed in the 06/01 release line. Anything still setting it (shell rc, CI secret, Docker ENV, k8s ConfigMap, .envrc) will silently stop influencing fast-mode routing. Sweep now while the rename is fresh.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Quiet behavior change — code keeps running but fast-mode routes differently than the team thinks. Twenty-minute grep beats a week of "why is this slow?".

example.code:
rg -F 'CLAUDE_CODE_OPUS_4_6_FAST_MODE_OVERRIDE' \
  ~/.zshrc ~/.bashrc ~/.envrc \
  .github docker k8s charts
# remove every hit, including secret stores

suggestions.title: Audit effort-label strings before bumping to Opus 4.8 default
suggestions.paragraph: Claude Code 2.1.154 renamed effort labels from Speed / Intelligence to Faster / Smarter and switched the default model to Opus 4.8 at high effort. Dashboards, log filters, or scripts that match on the old strings silently miss every new event.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Default-model jumps are loud (visible cost / latency change). Label renames are quiet — broken dashboards keep "working".

example.code:
# replace label strings in dashboards and scripts
rg -F 'Speed|Intelligence' .github scripts grafana datadog
# pin the CLI if 4.7 behavior matters
npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.149

suggestions.tiesTo: claude-code · v2.1.154 — Opus 4.8 default · Faster/Smarter rename

suggestions.title: Migrate Codex legacy profile configs before they hard-reject
suggestions.paragraph: Codex 0.134.0 deletes the v1 profile-config code path. The CLI now refuses to start on a legacy [profile.<name>] block in config.toml and points to migration docs. Migrate to per-profile files under .codex/profiles/ with --profile <name> at invocation time.
suggestions.whyItMatters: First user to upgrade after the next CI bump becomes the support ticket. Migrate ahead of the bump.

example.code:
# 1. split each legacy [profile.<name>] block into its own file
mkdir -p .codex/profiles
# .codex/profiles/work.toml: just the body of the old block

# 2. invoke with --profile
codex --profile work

suggestions.tiesTo: Codex · v0.134.0 — legacy profile configs rejected

suggestions.title: Bump the Agent SDK to ≥0.3.154 wherever you ship stdio MCP servers
suggestions.paragraph: Versions up to 0.3.153 tear down and re-spawn stdio MCP servers on every reconcile pass because of a config-equality false positive. Long-running hosts pay spawn cost on every reconcile. Bump unblocks both.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Symptoms are subtle (slow turn-around, climbing process count) but the fix is one version bump.

example.code:
pnpm add @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@^0.3.154
# verify in your MCP server logs that the server is no longer
# logging fresh startup messages on every agent reconcile

suggestions.tiesTo: Claude Agent SDK · v0.3.154 — stdio MCP servers reconcile fix

suggestions.title: Audit MCP servers for the 2026-07-28 RC breaking removals
suggestions.paragraph: The 2026-07-28 RC removes the initialize/notifications/initialized handshake, Mcp-Session-Id, ping, logging/setLevel, and notifications/roots/list_changed. It deprecates Roots, Sampling, Logging, and the HTTP+SSE transport. If you ship an MCP server, walk the surface and tag what needs to move before the stable cuts.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Twelve-month deprecation window sounds long until you remember SDKs adopt at their own pace and your users may bump faster than you do. Doing the audit now means migrations land on your schedule, not a support ticket's.

example.code:
# grep for the removed/deprecated surface in your MCP server
rg -F 'initialize|Mcp-Session-Id|logging/setLevel|roots/list_changed' src
rg -F 'resources/subscribe|resources/unsubscribe' src
# plan: move to subscriptions/listen + per-request _meta

suggestions.tiesTo: MCP · spec 2026-07-28-RC — stateless protocol + handshake removed

suggestions.title: Move repo-local skills under .claude/skills/ to skip the marketplace dance
suggestions.paragraph: As of Claude Code 2.1.157, anything under .claude/skills/ auto-loads as a plugin without marketplace registration. Use claude plugin init <name> to scaffold and stop maintaining a private marketplace just to share in-repo helpers across the team.
suggestions.whyItMatters: Removes the marketplace ceremony for skills that only matter inside one repo. Faster iteration loop, fewer moving parts.

example.code:
claude plugin init review-helper
# creates .claude/skills/review-helper/ with the right shape
# committed to the repo, every teammate gets it on next session
